long_biography.plain_text:
Long before he was known as an oligarch, Berezovsky studied applied mathematics and spent more than two decades researching optimisation and decision-making at the Soviet Academy of Sciences. Work on computerising AvtoVAZ exposed him to the car industry. When perestroika permitted private enterprise, he converted that technical relationship into LogoVAZ, which moved rapidly from software to Lada retailing.

Communications and access to government became mutually reinforcing assets in his public career. His interests included ORT television, TV-6 and the Kommersant newspaper. His political offices included deputy secretary of Russia's Security Council and executive secretary of the Commonwealth of Independent States. His alliance with the Kremlin collapsed after Vladimir Putin became president, and Britain granted him asylum in 2003.
